newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson up after it ends takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson up after it ends takeover bid.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co shares rose Wednesday after it dropped its bid to acquire Great Western Financial Corp as arbitragers unwound positions.

An arbitrager said people who were short Ahmanson were now covering by buying the shares. At the same time, people were shorting additional shares of rival bidder Washington Mutual Inc, which came under pressure. Great Western moved in tandem with Washington Mutual, the arbitrager said.
Ahmanson was up 1-3/8 to 41-5/8 in early trading. Washington Mutual was off 7/8 to 52-7/8 and Great Western was off 3/8 to 47.
In announced takeover deals, arbitragers generally sell shares of an acquirer when a deal is announced and buy stock of the target company.

Ahmanson withdrew its bid a day after the Delaware Chancery Court denied a motion by Ahmanson seeking to delay a vote on the Great Western merger with Washington Mutual, which Great Western has scheduled for June 13.

"They (Ahmanson) were basically a frustrated, hostile bidder whose bid was not worth significantly more (than Washington Mutual's)," said Steven Cohen, partner with Kellner, DiLeo and Co, a New York-based merger arbitrage firm.

"Courts are not inclined to interfere with merger plans or grant injunctions unless the complaining party has a very substantial claim," Cohen said. He said Ahmanson had "very little standing" with its complaint.
Cohen also said part of the reason for the rise in Ahmanson's stock could be attributed to speculation that Ahmanson might now become a merger target itself.
